I think they kind of happened at the same time? Like, I just stopped caring about all of it. I mean, that's why I came in, because I just barely care about anything that used to make me feel like myself. The dance class, hiking, trying new recipes... even game night, like I said. My mom used to put a box of baking soda in the fridge to stop smells, but I never remember to buy baking soda. I don't even bake. I tried making banana bread once during lockdown like everyone else, but I forgot to add the baking powder or whatever makes it rise, and it came out like a dense, wet brick. I ended up throwing it out for the birds, but even the crows wouldn't touch it. Crows are so smart, though. I watched this documentary where they showed crows solving puzzles to get food. They're basically little geniuses.

Well, it's been a while now. This has been going on since the robbery at that festival job I had... so about two years and three months ago. 

That festival was supposed to be so much fun, too. It was this big outdoor music and arts thing, and they had all these food trucks lined up. I remember there was this one truck that only sold gourmet grilled cheese sandwiches. They had one with brie and fig jam on sourdough, and the line for it was always like a mile long. The guy running it had this massive beard, like a lumberjack, but he was wearing a bright pink apron. I always wondered how hot it got inside those trucks during the summer. It has to be like an oven in there, right? Especially standing over a grill all day. My cousin worked in a kitchen once, and she said she used to put ice cubes in her bra just to survive the dinner rush. She eventually quit and went to cosmetology school. She cuts my hair now, actually, though she always cuts the bangs a little too short. I tell her just a trim, and then I walk out looking like I’m in a 90s punk band. 

But um... what was I saying? Oh, right, the timeline. Yeah, it's been about two years and three months since the festival thing happened. That's when all this started.

No, not really. I haven't noticed any days where I felt better, to be honest. It all just kind of blends together. 

Speaking of days blending together, I actually bought this giant wall calendar recently to try and keep track of things. It's one of those glossy ones with a different lighthouse for every month. I think it's... well, it's kind of both, maybe? Like I said before, I just barely care about the things that used to make me feel like myself. Dance class, hiking, trying new recipes... even game night. They all just sit there now like chores I keep putting off. Speaking of chores, my vacuum cleaner broke yesterday, and I'm so annoyed about it. It's one of those expensive cordless ones that you mount on the wall, and the battery just completely died. I only bought it like two years ago. I called customer service, and the guy on the phone—his name was Kevin, I think—was so unhelpful. He just kept telling me to check the filter. Like, obviously I checked the filter, Kevin. It's completely clean. I even washed it out in the sink and let it air dry on the dish rack for 24 hours just like the manual says. I saw this really cute bamboo dish rack at Target last week when I was looking for a birthday card for my aunt. She just turned 60, and she had this huge party at a country club, but I didn't go. I just sent a card with a gift card inside. I hate country clubs. The grass is always too perfect, and everyone wears those pastel polo shirts. My uncle used to wear those shirts, and he always popped the collar. It looked so ridiculous, especially because he was bald and sunburned all the time. But um, yeah, the lack of interest... it's just really hard to get up the energy to do anything, and I don't think I'd even have fun if I did.

Yeah, it's exactly like I was saying earlier. I just... I barely care about the things that used to make me feel like myself.
